articles.title: 🤖 Car Company's Robot Division Raises $900 Million; Nobody's Sure If They Make Cars Or Androids Anymore
articles.dateline: GUANGZHOU — reported from a factory that also, apparently, walks
paras: An electric-vehicle maker's robotics arm raised more than $900 million in its first outside funding round, valuing the walking-robot business at over $6.3 billion — proving that in 2026 the fastest way to raise money is to take whatever you already make and bolt legs onto it.

"We see enormous synergy," investors said, of a company that started with cars and pivoted to humanoids, presumably because the cars kept asking for it. Analysts note the humanoid-robot gold rush has officially reached the stage where a business can be worth billions before a single one of its products has folded a single towel.

articles.title: 💸 Chip Giant Now Just Funds Everything; Reportedly Backing An Open A.I. Push And Betting On A Search Startup Too
articles.dateline: SANTA CLARA — filed from atop the entire board game
paras: The world's dominant AI chipmaker is reportedly pouring billions into an open-weight AI push while weighing yet another large bet on an AI search company — reaching the final boss level of wealth, where you no longer pick winners, you simply own all of the players.

"We're enabling the ecosystem," the company said, of a strategy best described as buying every ticket in the raffle and then also hosting the raffle. Observers note that when the firm selling the shovels also funds the miners, prints the map, and owns the gold, it is less a gold rush and more a very polite monopoly wearing a friendship bracelet.

articles.title: 🎬 New A.I. Video Model Can Generate Anything; Your Eyes Are Officially No Longer Reliable Witnesses
articles.dateline: HANGZHOU — reported, allegedly, by a real human
paras: A tech giant unveiled a powerful new AI video model backed by billions in infrastructure, capable of generating convincing footage of events that never happened — a breakthrough that finally retires the ancient phrase "pics or it didn't happen," since now the pics prove absolutely nothing.

"The quality is astonishing," the company said, of a tool that can conjure video of anyone doing anything, forever complicating every group-chat argument that ends in "send proof." Media experts recommend a healthy new default: assume everything is fake until a notarized human swears otherwise, in person, in daylight.

articles.title: 🤝 A.I. Agents Get Their Own Official 'Foundation'; The Software Has Formed A Homeowners' Association
articles.dateline: THE STANDARDS BODY — reported through proper channels
paras: A cross-industry "Agentic AI Foundation" now counts more than 250 members standardizing how AI agents talk to one another — meaning the little autonomous programs running errands across the internet have officially organized, elected a board, and drafted bylaws.

"Interoperability is crucial," members agreed, of an effort to let every company's AI agents cooperate smoothly — which is either a triumph of engineering or the opening scene of the robots learning to coordinate. Historians will note that humanity's helpful little assistants first agreed on a standard, and then, presumably, on an agenda.

articles.title: 🔎 A.I. Agents Can Now Search The Web Themselves; The Intern Has Discovered Google And Will Not Stop
articles.dateline: THE CLOUD — reported between 4,000 open tabs
paras: A major cloud provider made live web search generally available to AI agents, letting them fetch current, cited information on their own — finally giving the tireless digital intern the one tool it was missing: the ability to look things up and come back very, very confident.

"It stays within your account," the company reassured, of agents that can now roam the live internet, gather facts, and cite their sources like an overachieving student. Users welcomed the accuracy while bracing for the inevitable day their assistant returns from the web with a fully-formed opinion and a reading list.

horoscopes.text: You will see a video today that never happened. Trust your gut, not your feed. Especially not your feed.
Your assistant will look something up and return alarmingly confident. Verify before you believe a single word.
Mercury has joined a foundation. Even the planets have bylaws now. Attend the meeting, or don't; it's minuted either way.

tech_tip: In 2026, 'pics or it didn't happen' is officially retired. New rule: assume the video is fake until a human you trust confirms it in person.
gadget_watch: Humanoid robots are now a multi-billion-dollar business before folding their first towel, and A.I. can generate video of literally anything — so enjoy a future that's equal parts walking helper and unreliable footage. Keep your receipts and your skepticism.
